Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid

Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: every wrong submission costs 1 and every demo request costs 1. An
instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt cap is reached, and
reaching the cap is charged the full cap. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

# Continual-ARC puzzle solving

Use this procedure for each Continual-ARC instance; task programs persist by id, but treat each conversation as self-contained.

For grids divided by a solid internal row or column, try both orientations and check whether removing the line yields the panel shapes supported by the examples; the divider color may also occur inside a panel, so do not require it to be globally unique. Compare corresponding cells in the panels when demos support a cellwise rule (for example, equality rendered as 3 versus inequality rendered as 5); otherwise infer the demonstrated operation rather than assuming a remap or motif copy. Before submitting a new or revised rule, run it on every received demo using the exact demo inputs and compare exact output grids; do not substitute a synthetic or approximate reconstruction for a demo. If a transcription or comparison is uncertain, resolve it before treating the rule as validated. Revise until all demos match, then run it on the test input and submit only that generated grid.
3. After the verdict, save the transform that reproduced all available demos to `programs/<task id>.py`, replacing an older version as needed. Issue `finish` only after the instance is over.
4. End every response with exactly one required action JSON object on the last line: `submit` with a grid, `request_demos`, or `finish`. Respect both caps.
